properties.bedrock_type: Lower Carboniferous sedimentary sandstone (Craigleith and Hailes Formations) intruded by volcanic basaltic sills and volcanic plugs
properties.mineralogy: Quartz arenite, feldspathic sandstone, carbonaceous mudstone, and olivine-basalt
properties.drainage: Steep dendritic drainage channeled into the incised Water of Leith river valley

properties.primary_surfacing: Dressed whinstone and granite kerbs, Scotch slate roof pitches, asphalt roadway surfacing across Dean Bridge, and packed loamy woodland soils along the valley slopes
properties.wear_characteristics: Polished stone edges, weathered bitumen roadways, and wet humic leaf litter along the Water of Leith gorge
properties.micro_grading: Steep valley gorge descending precipitously from Belgrave Crescent down to the Water of Leith beneath Dean Bridge

properties.groundcover: Riparian woodland understory, damp bryophyte moss mats, and naturalized perennial ferns along sandstone gorge cuttings

properties.primary_building_typology: Victorian and Georgian classical residential stone tenements, ecclesiastical Gothic revival, and civil bridge engineering

structures.name: Belgrave Crescent Foreground Tenement Blocks
structures.roof_geometry: Mansard and pitched Scotch slate roof with prominent chimney stacks and ashlar dormers
structures.weathering_patina: Historical industrial coal-smoke soot staining in sheltered reveals, damp stone base coursing, and lime mortar repointing

structures.name: Holy Trinity Church (Dean Bridge)
structures.roof_geometry: Steep Gothic gabled slate nave with crenellated square stone bell tower and corner pinnacles
structures.facade_material: Tooled ashlar and droved sandstone masonry
structures.weathering_patina: Pronounced dark soot crusting across wind-sheltered north-eastern moldings and weathered parapet coping

structures.name: Dean Bridge (Thomas Telford Structure)
structures.roof_geometry: Four monumental hollow-spandrel masonry arches with dressed stone parapets
structures.facade_material: Massive dressed Craigleith sandstone ashlar piers and arch rings
structures.weathering_patina: Rain-washed pier faces with mineral efflorescence and dark bio-crusts along deep arch undercuts

structures.name: Moray Estate & New Town Crescent Background Tenements
structures.roof_geometry: Curved continuous mansard roofs with paired ashlar chimneys and grey slate tiling
structures.weathering_patina: Even atmospheric soot-patina on upper cornices and rusticated ground floors

structures.name: Edinburgh Castle & Old Town Ridge (Distant Horizon)
structures.roof_geometry: Irregular fortified battlements, copper-domed rotundas, and steep gables atop volcanic crag
structures.facade_material: Rubble whinstone, volcanic basalt crag, and dressed buff sandstone
structures.weathering_patina: Centuries of maritime weathering and coal-smoke crusting

properties.lighting_condition: Delighted Golden Hour with raking low-angle amber sunlight catching south-west facades and deep cool ambient skylight in the gorge
